chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: The fights at Cafe Society
summary: Wartime audiences from the South sometimes started fights; once a man grabbed her until Canada Lee cooled things down, and Doc Cheatham skated over the bar.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I have some notes here about the days of Cafe Society. You mentioned Canada Lee; and were there some fights?

Oh, the fights. That was the most exciting thing. It was during the war. We had quite a few biased people to come up like from the South. They didn't understand a lot of things, like mixing and all that. Sundays you couldn't get in the club. They were outside standing and waiting to come in and like every other night there was a big fight. At this particular time I done a request of 'Roll 'Em' and it went over big. Some bright guy in the audience said, "Play it again!" He ran up and grabbed me and was holding me like this, so Eddie Heywood said, "Turn her loose! Man, man, man, turn her loose so she can take her encore!" You know, he stuttered. This guy wouldn't turn me loose so the fight started. Canada Lee happened to be in there and he cooled it off. In about 2 minutes we didn't have anybody there, not even the bartenders. So when Barney came back (Barney Josephson was away on vacation), "I heard you had another fight here. And you, Doc Cheatham, you were skating across my bar." Doc Cheatham said, "Man, I was trying to get to the door."
